name: Metaplanet
email_summary: Metaplanet cut its dilutive Series 10 warrant pool 41% but Capital Research quietly sold ~¥4.8B of stock, dropping below the 10% major-shareholder threshold.
bottom_line: Management's 41% cut to the Series 10 warrant pool is a genuine (if partial) governance win that reduces future dilution, but it was overshadowed by Capital Research's ~¥4.8B share sale that pushed its stake below 10% during a sharp stock decline. Net effect on thesis is mixed: incentive alignment improved, but a major institutional holder is trimming exposure and analysts remain cautious on residual dilution overhang.
source_conflicts: mNAV estimates diverge across sources: a Japanese retail-focused article implies ~0.66x (share price vs BTC value basis) as of Sep 15, while Seeking Alpha cites a 0.79x EV/mNAV discount the same day — likely different denominators (market cap vs enterprise value).

Share price snapshots conflict across trackers: Investing.com showed ¥293 (Sep 6), MSN showed ¥233 (Aug 10, stale), TradingView cached a figure of ¥461, while primary Japanese reporting places the close at ¥251 on Sep 15 and an intraday low of ¥232 on Sep 16 — the ¥251/¥232 figures from Japanese-language reporting citing TDnet disclosures are treated as most current.

updates.headline: Board cuts Series 10 warrant pool by 41%
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet's board resolved to cut the potential share pool under its 10th Series Stock Acquisition Rights by 41.1%, from 319,464,000 to 188,190,000 shares, lowering the conversion ratio from 696 to 410 shares per right. The company also scrapped a plan to transfer up to 90,000 rights into an employee incentive vehicle, opting to cancel them and design a new compensation plan with an external consultant instead.
updates.thesis_fit: Directly addresses the checklist's warrant/dilution concern by materially shrinking a controversial option pool that shareholders had criticized as amplifying dilution, though the pool remains over four times its original size per one analyst.

updates.headline: Capital Research stake falls below 10%, exits major-shareholder status
updates.what_happened: An EDINET change report (No.30) disclosed that Capital Research and Management Company's voting ratio fell from 10.63% (July 13) to 9.32% (as of Sep 8, 2026), causing it to lose "major shareholder" status. Aggregated sales between Aug 3 and Sep 8 totaled roughly 18.4 million shares (~¥4.84 billion), with the firm's holding dropping from 136,059,120 to 125,455,820 shares; Capital Research remains Metaplanet's largest overall shareholder by ranking despite the reduction.
updates.thesis_fit: This is precisely the checklist's flagged risk — a reduction by Capital Research/Capital Group — and it coincided with a roughly 25% share-price decline over the same window, raising concern about institutional confidence.

updates.headline: CFO reshuffle: capital markets head promoted to CFO
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet's board resolved an executive officer reshuffle effective September 11: outgoing CFO moved to a newly created Director of Administration role, while the former head of Capital Markets & IR, Shimpei Okuno, was promoted to Executive Officer, CFO. The company stated the change aims to strengthen finance and capital markets functions as the group's business scale expands.
updates.thesis_fit: A capital-markets-focused CFO could support better financing discipline going forward, but this is a routine leadership change rather than a capital-allocation or governance decision by itself.

updates.headline: Proposed capital reduction to ¥1 and new Hong Kong unit
updates.what_happened: Metaplanet's board proposed reducing capital stock from roughly ¥27.8 billion to ¥1 and zeroing capital reserves at a December 18, 2026 extraordinary general meeting, aiming to eliminate an approximately ¥1.8 billion accumulated deficit and create room for future dividends and buybacks. The board separately approved a wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary, Metaplanet Asset Management Asia Limited.
updates.thesis_fit: This is a procedural balance-sheet cleanup that could eventually enable buybacks or dividends per the checklist, but it has no immediate effect on BTC-per-share or dilution and its ultimate impact depends on future execution.

updates.headline: Seeking Alpha initiates cautious Hold on governance concerns
updates.what_happened: A Seeking Alpha analyst initiated coverage with a cautious Hold, noting that the September 11 Series 10 amendment reduced the warrant pool to 188.2 million shares but that this remains over four times the original pool size, and that governance and capital-structure concerns outweigh the stock's roughly 0.79x EV/mNAV discount.
updates.thesis_fit: Directly engages the checklist's concern about analyst critiques of dilution and governance, tempering the positive read on the warrant-pool cut.
